2. Fresh Claude Code worktrees created with --worktree or Remote Control worktree mode may lack Entire configuration and Claude hooks unless their settings are committed. Sessions then produce no checkpoints and commits receive no trailer. Add an appropriate doctor/status warning after verifying the actual configuration-loading and hook behavior.

- The original bloat is in prompt_attributions.user_added_per_file. Oversized historical blobs can make the checkpoint branch unpushable to GitHub.
- The PR adds checkpoint.CapPromptAttributions, a 4 MiB write-boundary cap, and a doctor repair command called shrink-checkpoint-metadata.

- Another clone can replay old bloated history onto a repaired remote through fetchAndRebaseRefCommon. Understand local-only commit boundaries and divergence before changing this path.
- The PR describes preserving other blobs, checkpoint IDs, commit metadata, configured signing, and history before the first affected blob. It also addresses independently repaired clones, tree equality, shared rewritten commits, and force-with-lease safety. Inspect the code and tests to establish which invariants apply to an automatic pre-push cleanup.
- Dedicated checkpoint_remote URLs have special handling in the PR. Do not assume that a normal tracking-ref approach covers every remote configuration.

- Decide whether the pre-push work should wait for the PR to merge or use an explicitly documented stacked dependency. Avoid duplicating the repair implementation or silently treating unmerged code as available on main.

- Report the commands run and their actual outcomes. Distinguish PR-description claims from locally verified behavior.

Communication and output:

content.text: I’ve finished the local and live-state review. I’m waiting for the two focused code reviewers to return, then I’ll give you the consolidated recommendation before rebasing onto Karthik’s exact PR head or editing anything.

The review supports building directly on Karthik’s PR at its current head, `d9c31d994`. The PR is still open and blocked only on review; its normal CI checks pass. Karthik explicitly said we could take both follow-ups, although that is contributor coordination rather than maintainer approval.

Both follow-ups remain unsolved:

- **Pre-push cleanup is needed.** The current recovery replays commits by hash. After clone A repairs history, clone B sees the repaired commits as unrelated and can replay the old oversized metadata. The fix must normalize the `entire/checkpoints/v1` replay, discard a replayed commit when the sanitized result already equals the repaired remote tree, and preserve only the real local suffix. It must run before OPF’s divergence check as well as in push-rejection recovery; changing only `fetchAndRebaseRefCommon` would leave the OPF path broken. It can support a dedicated `checkpoint_remote` safely by using the already-fetched ref and completing with an ordinary fast-forward push. Karthik’s doctor force-repair function should not be called from pre-push.
- **The worktree warning is needed, but its original wording is too broad.** Newer Claude Code versions inherit `.claude/settings.local.json` from the main checkout, so that part of the reported behavior is stale. Entire’s required `.entire` settings and project Claude hooks in `.claude/settings.json` can still be absent. In that state, shared Git hooks may look healthy while deliberately doing nothing, so sessions get no checkpoints and commits get no trailer.
- The warning should require positive evidence: a sibling linked worktree has active Entire settings and recognizable Entire Claude hooks while the current worktree is missing one or both. That avoids alarming ordinary repositories and intentionally disabled setups. A separate Remote Control clone cannot discover configuration that was never committed, so the remedy should also tell users to commit the two project files.
- An existing branch only adds `.entire/settings.local.json` to this repository’s `.worktreeinclude`; it is a local dogfood adjustment, not a general product solution. Open PR #2294 warns on commits without sessions, but missing Entire settings cause hook dispatch to exit before that warning, so it does not solve this case.

I’ll now stack our branch on the exact reviewed PR head and split implementation between the two focused agents. The pre-push work will add the shared v1 normalization/replay path and multi-clone regression coverage. The warning work will add one read-only diagnostic shared by human/JSON status and doctor, with linked-worktree, configured-worktree, disabled, and ordinary-repository coverage. I’ll integrate and review both patches, then run focused tests and the repository checks.
